scientific_question: Within the same immutable qualified 16-node state library, how far can the total-profile-water and upper-30-cm-water matching tolerances be tightened while retaining a materially different interface-adjacent H16?
rationale: E04 supports non-unique next interface exchange at the frozen 1e-4 cm aggregate-storage resolution.
Because E04's selected pair has a nonzero W_root30 mismatch, a stronger exact-valued sufficiency claim requires tighter state matching before another response probe.
The next step is therefore state-only and response-blind.

source_authority.source_artifacts: exact immutable D04, E01, E03, E03B and E03C artifact set already verified by E03D/E03E

selection.pair_scope: all distinct bit-nonidentical states in the deduplicated immutable library
selection.rung_rule: for each epsilon, a pair qualifies if both |ΔW_profile|<=epsilon and |ΔW_root30|<=epsilon and |ΔH16|>=0.01 cm
selection.selected_rung: tightest numeric tolerance with at least one qualifying pair; EXACT only if exact equality also has a qualifying pair
ranking_within_selected_rung: largest abs(delta theta16) as diagnostic tie-breaker
selection.persistence: persist all 16 H/theta values for the selected pair before any later response probe
selection.no_match: If no rung tighter than 1e-4 cm contains a qualifying pair, close E05 as CURRENT_LIBRARY_RESOLUTION_CEILING without changing source set or thresholds.

next_if_selected: Preregister a new fixed-Hc response probe using the immutable E05 pair, the same common-time reseed authority and the unchanged E04 forcing/response threshold.
next_if_ceiling: Move to a new independently controlled deep-state construction axis; do not continue retrospective state-library selection or relax H16.
controls: no response information in selection or ranking
no source artifact additions after result inspection
nonclaims: E05 is a state-space census only.
Failure to find a tighter pair is not proof of exact state sufficiency.
H16 remains a mechanistic discriminator, not an admitted reduced-state variable.
